verses.saheeh: By the dawn
verses.khattab: By the dawn
verses.jalalayn: By the dawn, that is to say, [by] the dawn of each day,
verses.romanUrdu: Kasam hai fajr ki

verses.saheeh: And [by] ten nights
verses.khattab: and the ten nights
verses.jalalayn: and [by] the ten nights, the [first] ten nights of Dhū’l-Hijja,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur dus raaton ki

verses.saheeh: And [by] the even [number] and the odd
verses.khattab: and the even and the odd
verses.jalalayn: and [by] the even, the pair, and the odd (read watr or witr, two [alternative] forms), the single,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jufft(even) aur taaq(odd) ki

verses.saheeh: And [by] the night when it passes,
verses.khattab: and the night when it passes
verses.jalalayn: and [by] the night in motion, falling or receding:
verses.romanUrdu: Aur Raat ki jabke woh ruksat ho rahi ho

verses.uthmani: هَلْ فِى ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٌۭ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ
verses.indopak: هَلۡ فِىۡ ذٰلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِّذِىۡ حِجۡرٍ ؕ
verses.transliteration: Hal fee zaalika qasamul lizee hijr
verses.saheeh: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?
verses.khattab: Is all this ˹not˺ a sufficient oath for those who have sense
verses.jalalayn: Is there in that, oath, an oath for one of sense?, [one of] intellect (the response to the oath has been omitted, that is to say, [it is to be understood as something like], la-tu‘adhdhabunna yā kuffāra Makka, ‘you will assuredly be chastised O disbelievers of Mecca!’).
verses.romanUrdu: kya ismein kisi sahib-e-aqal ke liye koi kasam hai

verses.uthmani: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
verses.indopak: اَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ ۙ
verses.transliteration: Alam tara kaifa fa'ala rabbuka bi'aad
verses.saheeh: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad -
verses.khattab: Did you not see how your Lord dealt with ’Ȃd—
verses.jalalayn: Have you not seen, [do you not] know O Muhammad (s), how your Lord dealt with ‘Ād,
verses.romanUrdu: Tumne dekha nahin ke tumhare Rubb ne kya bartao kiya

verses.saheeh: [With] Iram - who had lofty pillars,
verses.khattab: ˹the people˺ of Iram—with ˹their˺ great stature
verses.jalalayn: Iram — these were the former [people of] ‘Ād (Irama is an explicative supplement or a substitution, and it is treated as a diptote because it is a proper noun and feminine) — of the towering ones, that is to say, the tall ones — the tallest one among them would reach four hundred cubits —
verses.romanUrdu: Unchey sutuno waley Aad-e-iram kay saath

verses.uthmani: ٱلَّتِى لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ
verses.indopak: الَّتِىۡ لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِى الۡبِلَادِ ۙ
verses.transliteration: Allatee lam yukhlaq misluhaa fil bilaad
verses.saheeh: The likes of whom had never been created in the land?
verses.khattab: unmatched in any other land
verses.jalalayn: the like of which was not created in the land, in terms of their power of assault and strength,
verses.romanUrdu: Jinke manind koi qaum duniya kay mulkon mein paida nahin ki gayi thi

verses.transliteration: Wa samoodal lazeena jaabus sakhra bil waad
verses.saheeh: And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley?
verses.khattab: and Thamûd who carved ˹their homes into˺ the rocks in the ˹Stone˺ Valley
verses.jalalayn: and Thamūd, who hollowed, hewed, the rocks (sakhr is the plural of sakhra) in the valley, the Wādī al-Qurā, [rocks] which they used as dwellings,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur Samood ke saath jinhon ne wadi mei chattane tarashi thi

verses.saheeh: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes? -
verses.khattab: and the Pharaoh of mighty structures
verses.jalalayn: and Pharaoh, the one of the tent-pegs: he used to fasten four pegs and tie to these the hands and feet of those whom he tortured —
verses.romanUrdu: Aur mekhon waley Firoun kay saath

verses.saheeh: [All of] whom oppressed within the lands
verses.khattab: They all transgressed throughout the land
verses.jalalayn: those who were rebellious, became tyrannical, in the land,
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh woh log (thay) jinhone duniya kay mulkon mein badi sarkashi ki thi

verses.saheeh: And increased therein the corruption.
verses.khattab: spreading much corruption there
verses.jalalayn: and caused much corruption therein?, [by way of] slaying and otherwise.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur inmein bahut fasaad failaya tha

verses.saheeh: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
verses.khattab: So your Lord unleashed on them a scourge of punishment
verses.jalalayn: So your Lord poured on them a scourge of chastisement.
verses.romanUrdu: Aakhir-e-kaar tumhare Rubb ne inpar azaab ka koda barsa diya

verses.saheeh: Indeed, your Lord is in observation.
verses.khattab: ˹For˺ your Lord is truly vigilant
verses.jalalayn: Assuredly your Lord is ever on the watch, watching over the deeds of servants, nothing of which escapes Him, that He may then requite them for these [deeds].
verses.romanUrdu: Haqeeqat yeh hai kay tumhara Rubb ghaath(watchful) lagaye huey hai

verses.uthmani: فَأَمَّا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكْرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ
verses.indopak: فَاَمَّا الۡاِنۡسَانُ اِذَا مَا ابۡتَلٰٮهُ رَبُّهٗ فَاَكۡرَمَهٗ وَنَعَّمَهٗ ۙ فَيَقُوۡلُ رَبِّىۡۤ اَكۡرَمَنِ ؕ
verses.transliteration: Fa ammal insaanu izaa mab talaahu Rabbuhoo fa akramahoo wa na' 'amahoo fa yaqoolu Rabbeee akraman
verses.saheeh: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."
verses.khattab: Now, whenever a human being is tested by their Lord through ˹His˺ generosity and blessings, they boast, “My Lord has ˹deservedly˺ honoured me!”
verses.jalalayn: And as for man, the disbeliever, whenever his Lord tests him and honours him, with wealth and other things, and is gracious to him, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me’.
verses.romanUrdu: Magar Insan ka haal yeh hai kay uska Rubb jab usko aazmaish mein daalta hai aur usey izzat aur niyamat deta hai to woh kehta hai kay mere Rubb ne mujhey izzatdar bana diya

verses.uthmani: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
verses.indopak: وَاَمَّاۤ اِذَا مَا ابۡتَلٰٮهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهٗ ۙ فَيَقُوۡلُ رَبِّىۡۤ اَهَانَنِ ۚ
verses.transliteration: Wa ammaaa izaa mabtalaahu faqadara 'alaihi rizqahoo fa yaqoolu Rabbeee ahaanan
verses.saheeh: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
verses.khattab: But when He tests them by limiting their provision, they protest, “My Lord has ˹undeservedly˺ humiliated me!”
verses.jalalayn: But when he tests him and restricts his provision for him, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me’.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jab woh usko azmaish mein daalta hai aur uska rizq uspar tangg kar deta hai to woh kehta hai mere Rubb ne mujhey zaleel kar diya

verses.transliteration: Kalla bal laa tukrimooo nal yateem
verses.saheeh: No! But you do not honor the orphan
verses.khattab: Absolutely not! In fact, you are not ˹even˺ gracious to the orphan
verses.jalalayn: No indeed! — a disavowal [of this notion], in other words, honour is not about wealth, nor is there any humiliation in poverty, rather it has to do with obedience and disobedience [respectively]; but the disbelievers of Mecca unmindful of this. Rather they do not honour the orphan, they do not treat him with kindness, despite their wealth, or [it means that] they do not give him what is his due from an inheritance,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin, balke tum yateem se izzat ka sulook nahin kartey

verses.saheeh: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.
verses.khattab: nor do you urge one another to feed the poor
verses.jalalayn: and they do not urge, neither themselves nor others, the feeding of the needy;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur miskeen ko khana khilane par ek dusrey ko nahin uksatey

verses.saheeh: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,
verses.khattab: And you devour ˹others’˺ inheritance greedily
verses.jalalayn: and they devour inheritance (turāth means mīrāth) greedily (lamman), that is to say, voraciously, when they appropriate (lammuhum) the women’s and the young ones’ share of the inheritance together with their own share of it, or to their own wealth;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur Miras(inheritance) ka sara maal sameith kar kha jatey ho

verses.saheeh: And you love wealth with immense love.
verses.khattab: and love wealth fervently
verses.jalalayn: and they love wealth with abounding love, that is to say, greatly, and so they do not expend [any] of it (a variant reading in the case of all four verbs has the second person plural).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur maal ki muhabbat mei buri tarah giraftar ho

verses.uthmani: كَلَّآ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ دَكًّۭا دَكًّۭا
verses.indopak: كَلَّاۤ اِذَا دُكَّتِ الۡاَرۡضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا ۙ
verses.transliteration: Kallaaa izaaa dukkatil ardu dakkan dakka
verses.saheeh: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed -
verses.khattab: Enough! When the earth is entirely crushed over and over
verses.jalalayn: No indeed! — a deterrent for them from such [conduct]. When the earth is pulverised repeatedly, when it is shaken until every edifice has collapsed and is destroyed,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin jab zameen pai dar pai qoot qoot kar regzaar bana di jayegi

verses.transliteration: Wa jaaa'a Rabbuka wal malaku saffan saffaa
verses.saheeh: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank,
verses.khattab: and your Lord comes ˹to judge˺ with angels, rank upon rank
verses.jalalayn: and your Lord, that is to say, His command, and the angels arrive rank on rank (saffan saffan is a circumstantial qualifier, meaning ‘standing in rows’ or ‘made up of many ranks’),
verses.romanUrdu: Aur tumahra Rubb jalwa farma hoga is haal mei kay farishtey saff dar saff khade hongey

verses.uthmani: وَجِا۟ىٓءَ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بِجَهَنَّمَ ۚ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
verses.indopak: وَجِاىْٓءَ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍۢ بِجَهَنَّمَ ۙ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ يَّتَذَكَّرُ الۡاِنۡسَانُ وَاَنّٰى لَـهُ الذِّكۡرٰى ؕ
verses.transliteration: Wa jeee'a yawma'izim bi jahannnam; Yawma 'iziny yatazakkarul insaanu wa annaa lahuz zikraa
verses.saheeh: And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but what good to him will be the remembrance?
verses.khattab: and Hell is brought forth on that Day—this is when every ˹disbelieving˺ person will remember ˹their own sins˺. But what is the use of remembering then
verses.jalalayn: and Hell on that day is brought [near], pulled by seventy thousand sets of reins, each set of reins [pulled] by the hands of seventy thousand angels, as it groans and seethes in fury; on that day (yawma’idhin is a substitution for idhā, ‘when’, the response to which is [the following]) man, that is to say, the disbeliever, will remember, his prodigal conduct in it, but how will remembering avail him [now]? (the interrogative is meant as a denial, in other words, his remembering that will not be of any use to him).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jahannum us roz samnay le aayi jaeygi, us din Insan ko samajh ayegi aur us waqt us ke samajhne ka kya hasil

verses.saheeh: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."
verses.khattab: They will cry, “I wish I had sent forth ˹something good˺ for my ˹true˺ life.”
verses.jalalayn: He will say, as he remembers: ‘O (yā is for calling attention to something) would that I had sent ahead, good deeds and faith, for my life!’, [for] a good [life] in the Hereafter, or [it means] ‘during my life’ in the world.
verses.romanUrdu: Woh kahega ke kaash maine apni is zindagi ke liye kuch peshgi saman kiya hota

verses.transliteration: Fa Yawma izil laa yu'azzibu 'azaabahooo ahad
verses.saheeh: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment,
verses.khattab: On that Day He will punish ˹them˺ severely, like no other
verses.jalalayn: Then on that day none shall mete out (read yu‘adhdhibu) His, God’s, chastisement, that is to say, He shall not delegate it to any other;
verses.romanUrdu: Phir us din Allah jo azaab dega waisa azaab dene wala koi nahin

verses.transliteration: Wa laa yoosiqu wasaaqa hooo ahad
verses.saheeh: And none will bind [as severely] as His binding [of the evildoers].
verses.khattab: and bind ˹them˺ tightly, like no other
verses.jalalayn: and, likewise, none shall bind (read yūthiqu) His bind (a variant reading has yu‘adhdhabu, ‘[none] shall be chastised’, and yūthaqu, ‘[none] shall be bound’, so that the [suffixed] pronoun of ‘adhābahu and wathāqahu refers to the [chastisement and the binds of the] disbeliever, the meaning then being, ‘none shall be chastised as he shall, and none shall be bound as he shall [be bound]’).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur Allah jaisa bandhega waisa bandhne wala koi nahin

verses.saheeh: [To the righteous it will be said], "O reassured soul,
verses.khattab: ˹Allah will say to the righteous,˺ “O tranquil soul
verses.jalalayn: ‘O soul at peace!, [the one] secure, namely, the believing one.
verses.romanUrdu: (Dusri taraf irshad hoga) Aey nafsey mutmain(reassured soul/pious)

verses.saheeh: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him],
verses.khattab: Return to your Lord, well pleased ˹with Him˺ and well pleasing ˹to Him˺
verses.jalalayn: Return — this is said to it upon death — to your Lord, that is to say, return to His command and to His will, pleased, with the reward, pleasing, in God’s sight with your deeds; in other words [return O soul] combining both descriptions (both of which are circumstantial qualifiers). And it will be said to it at the Resurrection:
verses.romanUrdu: Chal apne Rubb ki taraf is haal mein ke tu (apne anjam-e-neik se) khush (Aur apne Rubb kay nazdeek) pasandida hai

verses.saheeh: And enter among My [righteous] servants
verses.khattab: So join My servants
verses.jalalayn: Then enter among My, righteous, servants!
verses.romanUrdu: Shamil ho ja mere (neik) bandon mein

verses.saheeh: And enter My Paradise."
verses.khattab: and enter My Paradise.”
verses.jalalayn: And enter My Paradise!’, with them.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur dakhil hoja meri jannat mein
